description:
About the Position

Poor air quality is the biggest environmental factor contributing to premature mortality globally. In the recent update to the global burden of disease, long-term exposures to fine particulate matter was estimated to contribute to 4.9 million premature deaths annually, with respiratory and cardiovascular diseases, cancer, diabetes and links to dementia being the main contributors.

Domestic solid fuel burning (in particular wood) is now the dominant source of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) in the UK (38% of the total in 2019). PM2.5 is one of the biggest areas of concern for air quality and human health in the UK and caused an estimated 33,100 excess deaths in 2019.

Research Focus

Fires can emit a wide range of pollutants into the gas and particle phases, including many organic compounds from the degradation of cellulose and lignin. Gas phase emissions of volatile organic compounds can react with atmospheric oxidants to form secondary organic aerosols (SOA). Many of the organic species emitted are known to be toxic, but little is known about the impact of atmospheric ageing on the toxicity of wood burning emissions.

The over-arching aims of this PhD studentship are to understand the formation and toxicity of SOA from domestic wood burning in the UK. The student will work within the NERC funded "CondensabLe AeRosol from non-Ideal Stove Emissions" (CLARISE) project. The student will carry out short deployments at the University of Manchester Stove Facility to collect samples and use state of the art analytical tools to determine the composition of the SOA formed. They will then use novel machine learning approaches to understand the impact of different burn and oxidation conditions on the toxicity of wood burning emissions.

Supervisors

  • Primary Supervisor: Professor Jacqui Hamilton (jacqui.hamilton@york.ac.uk), University of York (Wolfson Atmospheric Chemistry Laboratory, Department of Chemistry)
  • Academic Supervisor: Andrew Rickard (andrew.rickard@york.ac.uk), University of York

Research Themes

Air Quality, Atmosphere and Climate

Research Keywords

Air Quality, Atmosphere

Funding

This is a fully funded NERC Panorama DTP PhD studentship. The studentship covers tuition fees and provides a tax-free annual stipend (UKRI rate) for 3.5 years.

Eligibility and Requirements

  • Relevant degree in chemistry, environmental science, atmospheric science, or related field.
  • Strong interest in air quality and atmospheric chemistry.
  • Background in analytical chemistry or atmospheric science desirable.
  • Experience with machine learning or data analysis is an advantage.

How to Apply

Contact the primary supervisor Professor Jacqui Hamilton (jacqui.hamilton@york.ac.uk) for more information and to discuss the project.
